knowledge:
- key_parameters: de=A named numeric vector of log2 fold changes for differentially expressed genes, where names are Entrez gene IDs ;; all=A character vector containing the Entrez gene IDs of all genes profiled/considered in the analysis (background) ;; organism=A three-letter character string specifying the organism (e.g., "hsa" for Homo sapiens, "mmu" for Mus musculus) ;; nB=Number of bootstrap iterations used to compute the perturbation p-value (pPERT); use 2000 or more for accurate results ;; plots=Logical indicating whether to generate and save perturbation plots as a PDF ;; beta=A named numeric vector of weights for each type of gene-to-gene relation; if NULL, default weights are used ;; combine=Method to combine pPERT and pNDE, either "fisher" (default) or "norminv" (normal inversion) ;; data.dir=Directory where the processed pathway data is stored, required when using custom-generated pathway data
- alternatives: PathwayGuide=A commercial version of SPIA available from Advaita Bio that offers additional capabilities in visualization, speed, and user interface
- when_to_use: Use SPIA when you have performed a differential expression analysis (e.g., microarray or RNA-seq) and want to identify impacted signaling pathways by leveraging both the number of differentially expressed genes (over-representation) and their position/interactions within the pathway topology (perturbation).
- pitfalls: Outdated pathway data=The pre-packaged KEGG data in SPIA is outdated and provided for illustration only; users should download up-to-date KGML files and parse them using makeSPIAdata ;; Low bootstrap iterations=Using a low nB value (e.g., < 2000) can lead to inaccurate and unstable pPERT values ;; Incorrect gene IDs=SPIA strictly requires Entrez gene IDs; using other ID types (like probe IDs or Ensembl IDs) without mapping them first will cause the analysis to fail ;; Choice of combination method=Fisher's method can yield highly significant global p-values (pG) when only one of the two evidence types (pNDE or pPERT) is strong, whereas the normal inversion method ("norminv") requires both to be simultaneously low

workflows.name: standard_spia_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform Signaling Pathway Impact Analysis (SPIA) using pre-existing pathway data to identify significant pathways based on over-representation and topology perturbation.
input: DE_Colorectal (named numeric vector of log2 fold changes for differentially expressed genes, named by Entrez IDs)
ALL_Colorectal (character vector of Entrez IDs for all genes profiled on the platform)
workflows.stages: 1. Run the SPIA analysis using the spia function ;; 2. Visualize the pathway significance using the plotP function ;; 3. Recompute combined p-values using the combfunc function with the normal inversion method and adjust for multiple testing

workflows.name: spia_with_custom_kegg_data
workflows.intent: Parse up-to-date KGML (XML) files downloaded from KEGG to build custom pathway data and run SPIA analysis.
input: mydir (path to a directory containing downloaded KGML XML files for the organism of interest)
DE_Colorectal (named numeric vector of log2 fold changes for differentially expressed genes, named by Entrez IDs)
ALL_Colorectal (character vector of Entrez IDs for all genes profiled on the platform)
workflows.stages: 1. Parse the KGML files and generate SPIA-compatible data using the makeSPIAdata function ;; 2. Run the SPIA analysis using the spia function, pointing to the directory containing the newly generated data
